records.statement: Let G be any finite simple k-regular graph with exactly one common neighbor for adjacent vertices and two for nonadjacent vertices, S an induced support, x outside S, T=N(x) intersect S independent, W=N(x) minus S, s=|T| and U_w=N(w) intersect S. Every selected w in W meets T in at most one support vertex, and every u in T has exactly one such partner. P={w in W: |T intersect U_w|=1} has s elements and no edges to W; R=W minus P has nonnegative even size k-2s and induces a perfect matching, with every other W edge absent. Distinct selected w,z have |U_w intersect U_z|<=1; overlap1 forces nonadjacency, and matched R pairs have disjoint types. Thus a support type of size at least2 occurs at most once in W. These are conditional focal-neighborhood necessities, without uniform same-type profiles or automorphism; satisfying their qualified selector/matching constraints does not certify a full graph.

S is induced; x is outside S; T=N(x) intersect S is independent.
